passage:
Dear Tenzin,
I’ve been meaning to write since Sunday’s listening party. When I moved into the hostel in a new city, I ate dinner alone for a month. Then I found our fan group online and you, Mira and Joel wrote to me.
Someone drew my favourite character. Someone else shared a playlist when I had a bad week. On Sundays we listen together and talk about anything. When a group from another band mocked us, you said, “Let them be. We’re here for the songs.”
It’s the first place here that felt like mine. Thank you for that. ❤️
Sabina

qa.q: How long did Sabina eat dinner alone after moving to the hostel?
qa.a: Sabina ate dinner alone for a month after moving into the hostel.

qa.q: What was Sabina feeling before finding the fan group?
qa.a: Sabina was lonely in a new city, which is why the group felt like the first place that was Sabina's own.

qa.q: What did Tenzin's reply to the mocking group show about how the fan group works?
qa.a: Tenzin answered the mockery calmly and said they were there for the songs. It shows connection here does not depend on hating anyone.

qa.q: What might Joel or Mira have felt on hearing Sabina's message?
qa.a: They may have felt glad and a little proud that the group made a lonely person feel welcome. The letter thanks Tenzin mainly, so their feelings are a guess.

grounding: Shows a young adult finding connection and comfort in a fan community during a lonely time, without hatred of others.

passage:
Salma, you asked how the forum started. I’m Binita, and it was my first year at a university abroad, and I didn’t know anyone. My roommate was away most weekends, and evenings felt very long.
I started reading a forum for a detective series I loved. Then I posted a short story about one of the characters, and three strangers replied within an hour. One of them, Ines, started editing my spelling with jokes. After that we wrote stories together.
Once somebody posted hateful things about another series’ viewers, and the moderators deleted it and wrote, “We don’t do that here.” I stayed. I’m still there, and I’m still writing.

qa.q: What did Binita post that got replies from strangers?
qa.a: Binita posted a short story about one of the characters in the detective series.

qa.q: What was Binita feeling in the first weeks abroad?
qa.a: Binita felt lonely, since nobody was familiar and the evenings felt very long.

qa.q: What did the moderators' response to the hateful post show that helped Binita stay?
qa.a: They deleted it and said such posts were not allowed. That made the forum feel safe and showed connection did not depend on hating others.

qa.q: How might Ines have felt when the story-writing with Binita began?
qa.a: Ines probably felt welcomed and playful, since Ines replied so quickly and joked while helping with spelling. It suggests Ines also enjoyed finding someone to write with.

grounding: Shows a young adult finding connection and creative outlets in a fan forum during lonely first-year months.

passage: Parul's first months in Mumbai were lonely. Her paying-guest roommates worked night shifts, and her college friends were back in Indore. In the evenings she rewatched Lantern Street, an old animated series, and one night she found its fan group. Two thousand members drew fan art, wrote stories and shared tiny drawings of the lamp-lighter cat. Parul posted a sketch, shyly. Sarita, a fan from Thane, commented, 'This is SO good, you have to join the Sunday draw-along!' The group had one pinned rule: love what you love, don't trash what others love. Now, on Sundays, Parul sketched with twenty people on a video call, laughing about the cat. When Sarita suggested meeting at a comic fair with a few others, Parul checked who else was going, told her aunt, and went.

qa.q: What was the fan group's pinned rule?
qa.a: Love what you love, don't trash what others love.

qa.q: How did Parul feel when Sarita praised her sketch?
qa.a: Surprised and happy, less lonely, welcomed after months of isolation.

qa.q: What did Parul do to keep meeting fans safe?
qa.a: She checked who else was going to the public comic fair and told her aunt before going.

qa.q: What might the Sunday draw-alongs mean to Sarita?
qa.a: Sarita seems to enjoy bringing new people in and sharing the fun, so welcoming Parul likely felt good too.

grounding: A lonely young woman finds friendship and a creative outlet in a kind fan community.

'You're smiling at your phone again,' Lalremsiami said, sliding into the library seat. 'Who is it?'
'The Aizawl Eagles fan group,' Akash said. 'Remember I told you I had no friends my first term?'
'You ate lunch in the stairwell.'
'Yeah. Then I found this group. They post match memes, but also, when I said I was homesick, about ten people messaged me. One guy from Shillong sends me a good-morning sticker every day.'
'And they don't fight with other fans?'
'Nope. There's a rule: no trash-talking other clubs. When someone did it, the admin just removed the post.'
Lalremsiami grinned. 'I'm from Aizawl, you know. You never asked me about the Eagles.'
Akash stared. 'You're a fan?'
'Since I was six. Come to the screening on Saturday.'

qa.q: Where did Akash eat lunch in the first term?
qa.a: In the stairwell.

qa.q: What does Akash smiling at the phone show?
qa.a: Akash feels comforted and less alone, having found friends in the fan group during a homesick time.

qa.q: What makes Akash's fan group healthy?
qa.a: It offers friendship and support, and its rule against trash-talking keeps it from demanding hatred of other fans.

qa.q: How might Lalremsiami feel discovering Akash loves the Eagles?
qa.a: Lalremsiami is delighted and amused to find a shared love so close by, which is why Lalremsiami invites Akash to the screening.

grounding: A lonely student finds friends and comfort in a fan community that does not demand hatred of others.

passage: The year I failed my entrance exam, I barely left my room. My school friends had all gone to college. What saved me, honestly, was a fan forum for the Starbridge fantasy books. At first I only read theories. Then I wrote one about the dragon's missing egg, and people argued with me, kindly, for three days. A girl called Damini started messaging me every night about chapter drafts. We wrote a fan story together, forty thousand words. Nobody in the group was mean about other books, which surprised me; the moderator said, 'We're here because we love something, not because we hate something.' I'm Gurleen. I passed the exam the next year. Damini and her mother came to my first day at college, all the way from Ludhiana.

qa.q: How long was the fan story Gurleen and Damini wrote?
qa.a: Forty thousand words.

qa.q: How was Gurleen feeling in the year after failing the exam?
qa.a: Gurleen felt lonely and low, barely leaving the room while school friends went to college.

qa.q: What made this fan forum a healthy support?
qa.a: It offered friendship and a creative outlet, and its spirit of loving something without hating others kept it kind.

qa.q: What might the friendship have meant to Damini?
qa.a: Damini chose to message every night and travel from Ludhiana, so it clearly meant real closeness to her too.

grounding: A young adult finds friendship and creative comfort in a kind fan community during a lonely year.

passage:
Mentor's note, end of first semester.
Yogesh, first-year B.Sc., struggled after moving from Jalgaon. In August he ate alone and missed two mentor meetings. In October I noticed him drawing in the margins during our session: characters from an old animated series. He told me, a little shyly, that he had joined an online fan art group for it. A member there, Vasudha, from another college, had started a weekly drawing challenge, and twenty-odd members post every Sunday. "Nobody hates on anything," he said. "They just ask how you did the shading." He now runs a small sketch club at college with two classmates he met through the challenge. Next step: I've told him the art society's exhibition is in March and asked him to bring his Sunday drawings.

qa.q: How many mentor meetings did Yogesh miss in August?
qa.a: He missed two mentor meetings.

qa.q: How did Yogesh seem to feel about the fan art group?
qa.a: He felt welcomed and less lonely there, a little shy but pleased that people only asked about his shading.

qa.q: What did the mentor do next to support Yogesh?
qa.a: The mentor told him about the art society's March exhibition and asked him to bring his Sunday drawings.

qa.q: What might the weekly challenge mean to Vasudha?
qa.a: For Vasudha it may be a way to build a warm, creative circle, and seeing new members like Yogesh join probably feels rewarding.

grounding: The mentor's note shows a lonely first-year student finding friends, a creative outlet and comfort in a kind fan community.
